texts: Autumn storms come over the Cold Sea.
Early-winter storms come over the Cold Sea.

fields.sentence: Autumn storms come over the Cold Sea.

q2_gaps: a spatial path / superposition preposition on a motion event ('come OVER the Cold Sea'): the event-oblique `Location` is glossed 'in/at/on', while the preposition-named oblique is introduced for PPs naming what the activity is 'about or directed at' — neither branch explicitly covers a spatial 'over/across/through' path on an event
review.notes: The multi-word name is handled exactly per the Kestrel River pattern (one opaque symbol, Name, kind atom from the name-internal head, no `cold` modifier atom), and the storm subject correctly takes Patient as a non-volitional natural process rather than Agent.

fields.sentence: Early-winter storms come over the Cold Sea.

q1_issues.issue: 'over the Cold Sea' is slotted as Location, but Location is specified for in/at/on and the instruction set requires the preposition actually used rather than a near-fit named role, so the surface-preposition oblique (Over <event> cold_sea) is the licensed form; Location asserts the coming is situated at the sea rather than passing over it.

review.notes: The named place is handled exactly per the multi-word-name rule (one opaque symbol, Name string, separate kind atom, no modifier genus for 'Cold'), the bare-plural generic correctly becomes a distributing rule at (STV 0.9 0.9), and Patient on the storm's motion follows the non-volitional-natural-force branch of the intransitive test.

issues.reason: Thematic roles licenses a named role whenever the PP answers where/when/how/whence/whither and directs deciding by that question, Location's '(in/at/on ...)' gloss is illustrative rather than a closed list (the prompt's own reified postural takes a Location oblique for 'was lying across the threshold'), and only LocatedIn — the entity-side head — carries an explicit containment-only restriction, so (Location (sk_come $x) cold_sea) is licensed, true and well-typed.

new_gaps: the preposition boundary of the EVENT-side Location role: LocatedIn is legislated as containment-only with any other preposition kept entity-attached, but nothing states whether a non-containment locative/path preposition on an EVENT ('come over the sea', 'lay across the threshold') takes Location or the surface-preposition oblique (Over/Across <event> ...)
adjudication.notes: Location is entailed by the storms coming over the sea, so it loses specificity but asserts nothing false — not the 'situated at rather than passing over' over-assertion the reviewer describes. The rest is correct: name symbol plus separate kind atom, noun-modifier genus withheld, non-volitional-force Patient, bare-generic rule at (STV 0.9 0.9) with no QuantifierPhrase.
